title: The model reads the tool list and picks one

steps.label: Middleware hands the model its tool list

payload.name: find_donor
payload.description: Find a donor by exact email, or by name when the staff member names a person. Returns every match; ask the user when there is more than one.

query.description: An email address, or a first and/or last name.

payload.name: get_donation_history
payload.description: A donor's gifts, newest first. Use after find_donor gives you a donor id.

payload.name: create_receipt
payload.description: WRITE: sends a receipt. Only when the staff member explicitly asked, and only for a confirmed donation id.

steps.annotate: This list is sent with every request. The descriptions are the only thing steering the choice.

steps.label: Staff: 'Did Maria Alvarez give this spring?'

payload.content: Did Maria Alvarez give this spring?

steps.annotate: No email, a name. The find_donor description says names are fine, so the model has a match.

steps.label: Model weighs the three tools

payload.find_donor: matches: a person is named, no id yet
payload.get_donation_history: needs a donor_id I do not have yet
payload.create_receipt: a WRITE; nobody asked for a receipt

steps.annotate: A tool description is a product decision: it is what makes the model skip the write and start with the lookup.

steps.label: Model emits one tool call
steps.annotate: Validated against the schema before anything runs: query is a string of at least 2 characters.

steps.label: What a worse description would have done
steps.payloadTitle: Same request, description changed to 'Find a donor'

payload.problem: The model guessed an id. Nothing in the description told it to look the person up first.

steps.annotate: Write descriptions for the reader that matters: the model. Then watch, in Module 2, how hosts show the difference.
